newsitem.title: INDIA: India copper plummets but zinc, lead firm.
newsitem.headline: India copper plummets but zinc, lead firm.

text.p: Copper prices nosedived while zinc and lead remained firm on the local market on Thursday, with other base metals steady in a narrow band, dealers said.

Copper prices fell by 150 rupees at 13,500 rupees per quintal on unloading by local stockists after producers reduced prices. State-owned Hindustan Copper Ltd. has cut selling prices by 6,000 rupees per tonne for the second half of July.
"State-owned Hindustan Zinc Ltd. has hiked selling prices of zinc by 3,000 rupees per tonne which in turn triggered an uptrend in the open market," one broker said.
"Zinc prices moved up by 100 rupees to 8,250 rupees per quintal and the rise in zinc also dragged lead upward by 50 rupees at 4,150 rupees per quintal," he added.
Aluminium was quiet at 7,700 rupees per quintal as was tin at 29,000 rupees and nickel at 33,800 rupees per quintal.

"Hindustan Zinc has hiked selling prices on the back of an upsurge in the world market while Hindustan Copper has reduced prices amid lower offtake and rising competition from the private copper producers," said Sharad Parikh, president of the Bombay Metal Exchange.
